original_question: Determine whether there exists a countable group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II1 factor, and whether there exists an existentially closed II1 factor that is not isomorphic to any group von Neumann algebra.
target_in_paper: Section "Existential embeddings", Problem 14: Does there exist a countable group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II_1 factor? The draft's added second clause is not itself an official problem in the paper; the nearest separate group-von-Neumann-algebra question is Problem 38 in Section "Miscellaneous".
correct_elements: The draft correctly captures the main official open problem from the paper's "Existential embeddings" section: whether some countable group G has group von Neumann algebra L(G) that is an existentially closed II_1 factor. It also correctly focuses on group von Neumann algebras rather than on arbitrary II_1 factors.
missing_details: The paper's exact official target is only Problem 14; the added clause asking for an existentially closed II_1 factor that is not isomorphic to any group von Neumann algebra is not posed there as an open problem.
The notation L(G) should be identified explicitly as the group von Neumann algebra of a countable discrete group G.
The phrase "existentially closed II_1 factor" should be defined: a II_1 factor M is existentially closed if whenever M embeds into a II_1 factor N, the embedding can be made existential.

The nearby context defines an embedding M -> P to be existential by using a tracial ultrapower: there must exist an embedding P -> M^U extending the diagonal embedding M -> M^U, where U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter.
The ultrapower notation M^U and the role of the nonprincipal ultrafilter U are implicit in the draft and should be made explicit if the question is to stand alone.

Because the conclusion asks that L(G) be a II_1 factor, factoriality of L(G) is implicit; in group terms this forces the relevant group to be of the kind whose group von Neumann algebra is a factor (in particular, ICC), even though the paper does not add this as a separate hypothesis.

Immediately before Problem 14, the paper already notes that existentially closed II_1 factors exist; thus the open issue is not existence of such factors in general, but whether one can arise as a group factor.

There are no ambient field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or "for sufficiently large" parameters in this problem; the missing stand-alone data are purely operator-algebraic and model-theoretic definitions.
refined_question: Does there exist a countable discrete group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is an existentially closed II_1 factor, in the sense that for every embedding of L(G) into a II_1 factor M, that embedding is existential—equivalently, for a nonprincipal ultrafilter U, there exists an embedding M into the tracial ultrapower L(G)^U whose restriction to L(G) is the diagonal embedding?
justification: Problem 14 is the exact official formulation matching the first half of the draft. The second half is broader than the paper: the author explicitly states just before Problem 14 that existentially closed II_1 factors already exist, and the only later official question involving group von Neumann algebras is Problem 38, which asks whether an ultrapower M^U can ever be isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra. That is not the same as asking whether some existentially closed II_1 factor fails to be a group factor. So the narrow, paper-faithful refinement is to restate Problem 14 with the nearby definitions of existential embedding and existentially closed made explicit.
